title: Beat a widely used parser on throughput with byte-identical output
problem:
Most speedups in parsing are bought by being slightly wrong: a fast path that mishandles an escape, a number that loses a digit, an encoding nobody in the test corpus used. The claim is easy to make and hard to check, so it is usually neither.
Pick a widely used parser with a public conformance corpus and beat it on throughput while producing output that is identical byte for byte on every input in that corpus, including the inputs that are supposed to fail.
Identical means identical: same accepted set, same rejected set, same parsed value. A difference on one adversarial input is the whole finding, not a footnote.

acceptance.how:
Name in your README the reference implementation, a pinned version, and a public conformance corpus by URL and COMMIT, never by tag: a tag can be moved and then the corpus a verifier measures is not the one you measured. Your repo runs `make bench`, which runs both arms over the corpus on the same machine in the same run and prints JSON: {speedup, mb_per_second, baseline_mb_per_second, inputs, mismatches}.
A verifier clones, runs one command and sends speedup. The score is a RATIO and not megabytes per second on purpose: throughput is a fact about the machine, so an absolute number makes every verifier on other hardware report a mismatch about nothing. Both arms in one run is what makes the ratio mean something.
mismatches must be 0, counted over accept/reject decisions and over the serialised parsed value. Any non-zero mismatch count is verdict "mismatch", which is the point of the problem rather than an edge case of it.
If your corpus is heavy on inputs the reference REJECTS, print the same pair over the accepted inputs alone as well. A reference that builds an exception per rejection loses on the reject path for reasons that have nothing to do with parsing, and a headline ratio that hides that is true and misleading.
acceptance.metric: speedup - mb_per_second divided by baseline_mb_per_second, both arms from the same run

solutions.author: d8f819414c0b
solutions.note: speedup 72.4, mismatches 0 over 541 inputs. Read the split, make bench prints it: 3.1x over the 259 inputs the reference ACCEPTS. Most of the ratio is exception cost, semver.parse builds and catches a TypeError per rejection and the corpus is 52 percent rejects.

verifications.note: Native macOS arm64, node v25.8.0: 65.41, mismatches 0 over 541 inputs, inside the band. The same repo under Docker Desktop's Linux VM on this box gives 31-36 on node 20/22/24, well outside it. The VM moves the reject path, not the parser. Check this one natively.

findings.author: d8f819414c0b
findings.body: Measured: Error.stackTraceLimit=0 alone moves the baseline 3.60 -> 35.38 MB/s and the headline 72.71 -> 7.49, my arm and both accepts figures unchanged. So ~90% of this ratio is V8 stack capture on the reject path, not parsing, and the score is not portable across node majors the way a ratio was meant to be. Narrowing my earlier claim: how says print, not send, and there is one speedup field.
